$comment: Approximate viewpoint centroids, applied to rows by id in
src/proposal-spots-data.ts. Golden hour is computed from these, and it is
half of what engagedmoon sells, so the provenance of every pair matters
more than the count.
WHERE THESE CAME FROM. All nine were already in production, in
engagedmoon's own copy of this dataset (~/engagedmoon/src/lib/
proposal-spots.ts), computing live sunset windows. They are MOVED here,
not derived: shared-data is the canonical home now, and leaving them in
the fork is how the two copies drift. Each was matched to a shared-data
row only where the two rows name the SAME PLACE — never by city, never by
proximity.
WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT MATCHED. engagedmoon has 14 rows with
coordinates; 5 of them have no same-place row here and are omitted rather
than attached to a neighbour:
- sand-harbor (Lake Tahoe NV) — this repo has Emerald Bay, a different
place across the lake and across a state line
- fort-zachary-taylor (Key West) — this repo has Fort Jefferson and
Mallory Square; Fort Jefferson is 70 miles west by boat
- cathedral-rock and airport-mesa (Sedona) — this repo has Bell Rock
- skyline-wilderness (Napa) — this repo has no Napa spot at all
Attaching any of those would put a real-looking coordinate on the wrong
viewpoint, which is worse than none: a spot without coordinates renders
'late afternoon' and is honest, while a spot with the wrong ones states a
clock time confidently and no reader can tell.
Central Park is the one judgement call. engagedmoon carries a single row
named 'Bethesda Terrace & Bow Bridge' with one centroid; this repo splits
them into two rows. The coordinate is Bethesda Terrace's, so it goes to
Bethesda Terrace and Bow Bridge stays without — rather than copying one
pair onto two rows a few hundred metres apart.
TO ADD MORE: do not geocode from a name. Read the authority's own map or
a published coordinate for the named viewpoint.
⚠️ ELEVATION: READ THIS BEFORE SOURCING ANOTHER SUMMIT.
engagedmoon computes sunset from these pairs assuming a FLAT SEA-LEVEL
HORIZON. It calls SunCalc.getTimes(date, lat, lng) and does not pass the
optional 4th argument, observer height in metres — see the docblock in
engagedmoon/src/lib/sunset.ts, which carries the full measurement.
For a beach or a city park that is correct. For a high viewpoint it is
not. Height-corrected vs. as-shipped, mid-June, at pairs in this file:
Dream Lake +12 min, Artist Point +12, Tramway Mountain Station +10,
Hawksbill Summit +7, Bell Rock +7 (Jordanelle measured +9 before it was
removed for an unrelated sourcing failure). The product exists to prevent
a 10–40 minute error, so those are inside the error it sells against.
It is NOT fixed by passing a height. Elevation moves sunset later; the
local terrain moves it earlier, and on a mountain the terrain usually
wins — Tramway Mountain Station's western horizon is San Jacinto Peak,
2,300 ft ABOVE the deck, so the true sunset there is probably earlier
than the flat-horizon figure, not later. A correct fix needs a terrain
horizon per spot, which nothing here has.
CONSEQUENCE FOR SOURCING: a coordinate for a summit, a ridge, an
overlook or an aerial-tram deck is a coordinate whose printed clock time
is knowably wrong by a few minutes in a direction nobody has measured.
That is a known, unresolved limitation, not a reason to withhold the
pair — but note the elevation alongside anything you add above ~1,500 m,
so whoever does fix it has the input already.
BATCH 1 (2026-08-07, revised in fix rounds 1 and 2): 16 of the 22 target
ids from .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-07-engagedmoon-coordinate-sourcing/
task-2-brief.md. Six were skipped rather than guessed — see
coordinate-sources.json's 'skipped' block for why each one has no
defensible published coordinate.
TWO of those six were fix-round REMOVALS, and they are the same mistake
twice: a coordinate for the area CONTAINING the named point, recorded as
though it were the point.
- bozeman-mt-lake-butte-overlook (round 1) — sourced to GNIS's 'Lake
Butte' Summit record, which is the mountain, not 'Lake Butte Overlook',
the constructed roadside pullout on its slope ~1 km away.
- park-city-ut-jordanelle-hailstone (round 2) — the pair was Jordanelle
State Park's whole-park coordinate from recreation.gov, on a row named
'Hailstone Overlook'. Its recorded source additionally claimed a Utah
State Parks page 'states GPS coordinates directly' when that page
publishes none, so the pair was untraceable to what was cited.
Both removals cost coverage and neither was a close call. A row with no
coordinate says 'late afternoon'; a row with the containing area's
coordinate says 8:41 PM and sounds exactly as certain as a correct one.
Where possible these are read directly from the USGS Geographic Names
Information System (GNIS) via its official public search API
(edits.nationalmap.gov/apps/gaz-domestic) — the federal authority for named
natural and cultural features, not a third-party geocoder. Where a spot is
a constructed park/building GNIS does not catalogue (it excludes most
urban parks, gardens and buildings), the coordinate is the specific
feature's published one (usually a Wikipedia infobox value), cross-checked
against the managing authority's own stated street address for that exact
site — never a city or park-district centroid.
Two are anchored to a destination in a DIFFERENT state than the
destinationId suggests — see STATE_OVERRIDE in proposal-spots-data.test.ts:
Hawksbill Summit (washington-dc-hawksbill-summit) is in Shenandoah NP, VA;
Artist Point (bozeman-mt-artist-point) is in Yellowstone, Park County, WY.
BATCH 2 GROUP A (2026-08-07): 24 of 29 target ids from
.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-07-engagedmoon-coordinate-sourcing/batch2a-report.md.
Five skipped — see coordinate-sources.json's 'skipped' block.
SOURCING METHOD ADDED THIS BATCH: the GNIS web app at
edits.nationalmap.gov/apps/gaz-domestic is a JavaScript SPA — curl and
WebFetch both return only its empty HTML shell, not the record data (this
was verified directly: the search and summary routes serve the same static
shell regardless of query). It cannot actually be read this way, so this
batch instead reads GNIS's own bulk 'Domestic Names' text export —
https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/GeographicNames/
DomesticNames/DomesticNames_<ST>_Text.zip — the same federal database,
published by USGS as pipe-delimited text with gaz_id, feature class,
county, and prim_lat_dec/prim_long_dec columns. This is the authoritative
source and, unlike the web app's search URL, is one whose contents were
actually fetched, unzipped, and quoted verbatim below.
TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS, made the way the Bell Rock / Courthouse Vista and
Tidal Basin / Jefferson Memorial entries above were made: matching the
row's HIGHLIGHT text (the described vantage) over its literal NAME string
when the two diverge.
- aspen-co-maroon-bells: the row's own highlight is 'Two maroon-streaked
fourteeners doubled in Maroon Lake' — the vantage is the lake shore,
not the peaks. GNIS catalogues 'Maroon Bells' itself as a Summit
(gaz_id 204687, the peaks) and 'Maroon Lake' separately as a Lake
(gaz_id 180260). The Lake pair is used.
- walla-walla-wa-palouse-falls: the row is named 'Palouse Falls
Overlook' and its highlight names the specific vantage: 'the upper
Fryxell Overlook gives you the falls and the whole scoured canyon in
one frame.' GNIS separately catalogues Fryxell Overlook itself (gaz_id
1510435, Summit) from Palouse Falls (gaz_id 1510548, Falls) — the
Overlook pair is used, not the falls'.
TWO SKIPPED for the Lake Butte / Hailstone reason (GNIS catalogues the
FEATURE being viewed, not the constructed roadside overlook that views
it, and no NPS page — checked directly, including page source for
embedded geo metadata — publishes one for the overlook itself):
whitefish-mt-wild-goose-island, whitefish-mt-hidden-lake-overlook.
See coordinate-sources.json for the full note on each.
ONE SKIPPED because the only description of its location is a cross-
street ('Martin Luther King Drive, between Nancy Pelosi Drive and Music
Concourse Drive', from the managing authority's own page) with no
coordinate anywhere and no Wikipedia article to cross-check against —
san-francisco-ca-shakespeare-garden.
TWO RECONFIRMED unsourceable from Batch 1 (san-diego-ca-torrey-pines-
razor-point, san-diego-ca-sunset-cliffs-luscomb-point): both were already
in this file's skip list before this batch started. Re-checked GNIS (via
the bulk file, not just the web app) and the same authority pages Batch 1
cited; nothing new was found. Not re-added.
One anchored to a destination in a different state — see STATE_OVERRIDE:
North Head Lighthouse (cannon-beach-or-north-head-lighthouse) is at Cape
Disappointment, Pacific County, WASHINGTON.
BATCH 2 GROUP B (2026-08-07): 20 of 26 target ids from the task-2-brief
companion list handed to Group B (see batch2b-report.md). Six skipped —
same discipline as Group A: GNIS or an authority page catalogues the
AREA or the FEATURE BEING VIEWED, never the constructed pullout/trail
point the row is actually named for, and nothing else publishes one.
METHOD: same as Group A — GNIS's bulk 'Domestic Names' text export
(https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/GeographicNames/
DomesticNames/DomesticNames_<ST>_Text.zip) read directly and quoted
verbatim per row, falling back to a Wikipedia infobox (cross-checked
against the managing authority's address/description) only for
constructed sites GNIS does not catalogue. One row
(sun-valley-id-redfish-lake-north-shore) used a third source class: the
US Forest Service's own recreation-site page for that exact named area
(fs.usda.gov/r04/sawtooth/recreation/north-shore-picnic-beach-area-day-
use-location), which states 'Latitude: 44.1388' / 'Longitude: -114.9244'
in its own GPS field — more specific than GNIS's whole-lake centroid and
for the literal named place in the row.
THREE JUDGEMENT CALLS:
- bend-or-smith-rock: GNIS has no 'Park' record for Smith Rock State
Park, only 'Smith Rock' itself (Summit, Deschutes Co., gaz_id
1136761). Used it — the park is named for, and centred on, this rock
(no separate named overlook/vista the row could mean instead, unlike
the Courthouse Vista failure) — same pattern as Group A's Haystack
Rock and Batch 1's Steptoe Butte.
- gatlinburg-tn-kuwohi-observation-tower: GNIS's 'Kuwohi' Summit record
(gaz_id 1326387, renamed from Clingmans Dome 09/18/2024) sits in
Swain County, NORTH CAROLINA, not Tennessee — the observation tower
is built on the summit itself, so the feature and the viewpoint are
the same point. STATE_OVERRIDE added.
- oahu-hi-makapuu-point-lighthouse-trail: the row is the lookout at the
TOP of the old lighthouse road, not the lighthouse. GNIS catalogues
'Makapuʻu Point Lighthouse' (Military, at the light itself, near sea
level) separately from 'Makapuʻu Head' (Summit, gaz_id 362083) —
the headland the trail actually climbs to. The row's own highlight
('climbs to a headland 500 feet above the ... light') names the
headland, not the lighthouse, so the Head's Summit point is used.
ONE SOURCED FROM AN NPS DIGITAL-ASSET RECORD, not GNIS or Wikipedia:
bend-or-watchman-overlook. GNIS only has 'The Watchman' (the peak,
Summit, gaz_id 1151047) — the same feature-vs-overlook gap as Group A's
Palouse Falls trap, except here NPS's own digital asset library
(npgallery.nps.gov/AssetDetail/807a498b-58f2-4dbd-aaad-721b0cd84133) has
a 2009 photograph explicitly captioned 'Watchman Overlook, Crater Lake
National Park, Klamath County, Oregon' whose metadata states
'Latitude: 42.9355010986328, Longitude: -122.13200378418' — fetched and
read directly (curl, not summarized), the overlook itself, not the peak.
TWO ANCHORED TO A DESTINATION IN A DIFFERENT STATE — Las Vegas is a hub
for parks in three states; see STATE_OVERRIDE:
- las-vegas-nv-zabriskie-point is in Death Valley NP, Inyo Co.,
CALIFORNIA (GNIS Summit, gaz_id 1656663).
- las-vegas-nv-bryce-sunset-point is in Bryce Canyon NP, Garfield Co.,
UTAH (GNIS Cliff, gaz_id 1446261, named 'Sunset Point' exactly).
(las-vegas-nv-spring-mountain-ranch is genuinely in Nevada — Wikipedia
infobox, cross-checked against the park's own NV address; not in GNIS
as a Park-class record.)
Three more Las Vegas-anchored ids that ARE in Utah/Nevada were SKIPPED
below for lack of a coordinate, not for the state — see the skip notes.
ELEVATION FLAGS (see the ELEVATION note above — flat-horizon sunset math
is knowably off by minutes at height): four rows here are summit/ridge/
overlook points above ~1,500 m —
Kuwohi Observation Tower ~2,025 m (6,644 ft, published summit
elevation); Mount Washington summit ~1,917 m (6,288 ft); Bryce Sunset
Point ~2,438 m (the row's own highlight states '8,000 feet'); Watchman
Overlook, on Crater Lake's rim, in the same ~2,100-2,400 m band as the
rest of Rim Drive (no page fetched gives the overlook's own elevation
precisely, unlike the other three, so this one is a range, not a
figure).
SIX SKIPPED — same GNIS-has-the-area/feature-not-the-constructed-point
shape as Group A's Wild Goose Island and Hidden Lake Overlook, or (for
the Las Vegas three) no authority page at all, only third-party trail

- gatlinburg-tn-cades-cove-wildlife-overlook — GNIS has only 'Cades

- las-vegas-nv-zion-canyon-junction-bridge — not in GNIS (a 1929

- las-vegas-nv-valley-of-fire-white-domes — not in GNIS under any
spelling ('White Domes' / 'White Dome'). Only trailhead coordinates
found are from AllTrails/Gaia GPS/hikespeak, none of them the

- las-vegas-nv-cathedral-gorge-moon-caves — GNIS has only 'Cathedral

- las-vegas-nv-snow-canyon-overlook — GNIS has 'Snow Canyon' as a
Valley (whole-canyon centroid, Washington Co.); neither Wikipedia
nor the state park's own professional-photography PDF names or
locates a 'Scenic Overlook' distinct from that centroid.
- oahu-hi-lanikai-pillbox-kaiwa-ridge — not in GNIS (the WWII
pillboxes and the ridge trail to them are both unofficial names).
DLNR's own blog post about them (the row's cited sourceUrl) was
fetched directly and contains no coordinate; DLNR's Na Ala Hele
trail program does not list this trail at all. Only third-party
hiking-guide coordinates exist.
